variant_desc: tag inside scattered node (pointer-chase DRAM miss per probe) -> 16-bit tag in upper bits of pointer (probe avoids deref on miss) (variant 1: seed=43, n_scale=0.5x)
source_citation: Birler, Schmidt, Fent, Neumann. CedarDB DaMoN'24 hash-table paper; https://cedardb.com/blog/efficient_hashtables/
novelty_rationale: Tests recognition that a 16-bit per-pointer fingerprint can be folded into the unused upper bits of a 64-bit pointer (4-level paging makes them sign-extension copies of bit 47). The slow version has to dereference the pointer to a scattered node just to READ its fingerprint, which is a DRAM round-trip; packing the tag in the pointer lets the could-contain check use the already-loaded word. Compilers never invent pointer-tagging schemes because they cannot prove the application never inspects raw pointer bits. Caveat: Intel 5-level paging (Ice Lake+) reduces usable upper bits from 16 to 7 — the pattern still applies, just choose a narrower tag.
